#133326. Breaking: How Sculpt Became the Fitness Space’s Buzziest—and Vaguest—Workout

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2193 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: How Sculpt Became the Fitness Space’s Buzziest—and Vaguest—Workout

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2193 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By definition, the term sculpt means making something by carving stone or molding clay.
  • Over the years, however, the term has also become ubiquitous in fitness culture.
  • Now, the term is prolific in fitness classes and social media alike, that the meaning is a bit murky—which begs the question, what does “sculpt” really mean in the context of exercise?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By definition, the term sculpt means making something by carving stone or molding clay. It’s an art form, a manipulation of material to achieve a desired end result that’s aesthetically appealing.

Over the years, however, the term has also become ubiquitous in fitness culture. We talk about sculpting one's back or legs, implying some kind of crafting of muscles, as if treating the human form like a sculpture. In fact, check the group class schedule of any gym these days, and you’ll likely spot the term “sculpt” appear somewhere on the lineup—directing toward some variation of a Pilates mat or strength training class, often involving lower weights and higher reps.

Now, the term is prolific in fitness classes and social media alike, that the meaning is a bit murky—which begs the question, what does “sculpt” really mean in the context of exercise? Is it a legitimate term or nothing more than strategic marketing language?

The exercise term actually dates back decades, with the first mentions appearing in fitness publications in the late 1970s. “It comes out of bodybuilding culture, which became more prominent in that period […] and you started to see the term ‘body sculpture,’” says Natalia Mehlman Petrezela, PhD, a historian and author of Fit Nation: The Gains and Pains of America’s Exercise Obsession. And while there’s no clear record of who coined the term in a fitness context, there is speculation that it may have been inspired by German strongman Eugen Sandow (often called the "father of modern bodybuilding"), who referenced Greco-Roman sculptures as examples of the “ideal” physique in the late 19th century.

According to recent reports, in the 1980s, the idea of sculpting your muscles started to become much more mainstream, with the rise of aerobics, toning workouts, and fitness videos, claims physical therapist and trainer Shannon Ritchey, PT, DPT, founder of Evlo Fitness. As instructors began using the term to describe and market workouts designed to shape and define specific muscles, “sculpting” became part of the everyday fitness vocabulary.

Sources indicate that the term also taps into something more personal: this idea that we have the power to change the shape of our own physiques. “I think that it really gained momentum because one, it kind of speaks to the artistry of the body or the artistry of fitness. Also, there's so much individual agency in this,” says Petrezela. “It isn't about you just having the right genetics. Instead, you as an artist have the power to sculpt your own body.”.

In the 1990s, however, the revered muscular look brought about by ’80s fitness culture made way for a celebration of thinner, more waifish bodies. “There was—and this is still the case—a lot of fear around getting too bulky,” notes Petrezela. The term sculpting, however, molded into a promise of strength training without gaining too much muscle, which felt more palatable to women who feared such a physique.

“What's interesting is that we've changed the language over the years, but we're still selling women a very similar idea: that certain exercises will create a long, lean, toned appearance, while others will make them bulky,” notes Ritchey.

It has been revealed that if you worked out in the 2010s, you probably remember “sculpt” becoming a fixture of the boutique fitness boom. Still, while studio culture has waxed and waned over the last 20 years, the term has only gained traction, popping up across social media and on class schedules everywhere (think Pilates sculpt, yoga sculpt, and seemingly endless variations), notes Laura Girard, CPT, a NASM personal trainer and co-host of the Fit Literate podcast.

Girard speculates that the popularity of sculpt classes may be buoyed by the widespread craving for more community in a post-pandemic world. After all, group fitness can be a fantastic third space. But there's another reason “sculpt” makes for such an appealing class name: It signals a particular kind of workout experience. Girard has observed “sculpt” used “almost like a dog whistle that [suggests] this class is going to be friendly for women and not scary, but still intense,” she notes.

In a recent development, there's an aesthetic appeal, too. Petrezela believes the term’s resurgence of sorts has to do with how weightlifting and building muscle are very much having a moment, yet longstanding fears around getting “bulky” haven’t entirely disappeared. “It doesn't hurt that we are in a very, very image-driven moment in fitness culture,” she says. “We're not just looking at the images in magazines that come out once a month, but our [social media] feeds are nonstop bodies all day—many of which are shared by influencers who have their own aims for how you can sculpt a body that looks just like theirs, or so they say.”.

Recent findings suggest that if you were to ask 10 different people on the street what a “sculpt class” is, you may get 10 different answers. To some, sculpt is synonymous with a mat Pilates routine, to others it might be a strength-training session, and to others it might be a yoga practice involving light dumbbells. So, can all of these workouts really fall under the same umbrella? And when a class promises to “sculpt,” is that an actual measurable result your muscles can deliver—or a feeling the name is designed to sell?

According to the experts, it’s largely the latter. “In a world where two things are popular—strength training and being very thin—’sculpting’ seems to be an appealing middle ground from a marketing perspective,” claims Ritchey. “It promises ‘long, lean muscle tone’ without the perceived risk of building too much muscle.”.

She adds that “sculpt” is often used interchangeably with “toning,” which she describes as a “made-up term” that typically refers to changing your body composition (a.k.a., reducing fat and building muscle).

In a recent development, because there's no single definition, what you actually do in a sculpt class can vary considerably. Still, Girard notes many sculpt classes share certain characteristics: lighter weights, choreography-inspired movements, and a lot of mat work. She also notes that while exercises are often fatiguing (think: that familiar muscle-burning sensation), they’re not necessarily pushing you to muscle failure via progressive overload (which is necessary for hypertrophy, or muscle-building).

It has been revealed that ritchey, who taught a sculpt class years ago, recalls using dumbbells and bodyweight for high reps. “We would do an entire three- to four-minute song of squats and lunges. That’s likely over 100 squats in a row, which burns and feels hard,” she says. Of course, it’s certainly possible to promote muscle-building with a low-weight, high-rep range, granted the programming is intentional. “But we know that if you could physically do more than about 30 reps in a row, the load is too light to build muscle.”.

It’s important to note that a workout doesn't have to maximize muscle growth to be worthwhile. Certain sculpt classes can offer other benefits, from muscular endurance to simply providing motivation and enjoyment of exercising, often in a group setting. But if your primary goal is to significantly increase muscle size or change your body composition, not every sculpt class will provide the progressive resistance training needed to make that happen.

According to recent reports, that’s where experts say the “sculpt” terminology can get confusing or misleading for some people. Girard fears that the language surrounding sculpt workouts reinforces misconceptions about women's bodies and what exercise can realistically change. “Sculpt as a verb is not a thing we can do to our bodies,” she notes. “We can gain or lose muscle. We can gain or lose fat, but that's more the role of nutrition. But we can't control how those muscles look.”.

In other words, there's no special exercise technique that creates “long, lean” muscles instead of so-called “bulky” ones. Your genetics influence your muscle shape, while your training can affect how much muscle you build. And the workout's name doesn't change those underlying principles.

What’s more, at a time when there’s seemingly no consensus on how to talk about bodies or fitness in an empowering, nonoffensive way, Girard sees the term “sculpt” as potential coded language. While we may have mostly done away with, say, “bikini body shred” language in 2026, she fears that this nebulous term may be subliminally hinting at the same idea.

And while there's absolutely “nothing wrong with having aesthetic goals,” Ritchey stresses, “women deserve accurate information about how to achieve them.” If body recomp is their goal, they would have more success lifting close to failure and focusing on diet.”.

Industry observers note that ultimately, your muscles don’t know whether you’re in a sculpt class or a traditional strength workout. Instead, they respond to the resistance, effort, and progression involved.

Industry observers note that “It’s funny because while all these trends come and go—and we will see sculpt come and go, too—the science never changes,” Ritchey notes. “People just aren’t patient enough with the basics, so they jump on the latest trend thinking it will finally be the golden ticket to seeing results.”.

Because “sculpt” has no one definition, the quality, intensity, and overall experience of classes bearing the name can vary widely, too.

Industry observers note that beyond the workout itself, Girard points out that some sculpt classes can come with an unspoken expectation about who belongs in the room. As she’s observed: “These classes tend to be a self-selecting in-group. You may only see one type of body, or one specific outfit [...] That doesn’t mean it’s wrong or bad to be in a different outfit or in a different body, but it sure can feel that way.”.

Sources indicate that of course, there are also plenty of classes with “sculpt” in the name that are fantastic, inclusive workouts. This all boils down to the instructor, methods, and specific exercises they choose to incorporate—along with the type of community they cultivate. And, in many cases—particularly with larger studios or gyms—instructors have no say in what their class is actually called. “A lot of times, they're just doing what's trending to get people in the door,” claims Girard.

It has been revealed that so if you’ve been curious to try a new sculpt class at a local studio—by all means, go for it. Just be sure to go into it with eyes wide open, and give yourself permission to stop or pause or walk away if it doesn’t feel like a productive or positive environment for you. Pay attention to how the workout feels, how the instructor coaches, and whether the environment makes you feel welcome. One potential red flag? Aggressive “bikini body” messaging or marketing that frames building muscle as something to avoid. As Girard emphasizes, “It is definitely, definitely is not.”.

As the experts agree: Finding a form of movement you enjoy is the most important ingredient for establishing a healthy, consistent fitness routine. “My advice would be to ask yourself why you're doing these classes. Is it because you genuinely enjoy them? Or is it because you believe the burning sensation means you're toning and sculpting your muscles? Because those are two very different things,” says Ritchey.

Have a sculpt workout you absolutely love? That’s wonderful, too. Finding movement you genuinely enjoy is one of the best ways to build a fitness routine you'll actually stick with. The notable thing is understanding what you're getting out of it—and whether that aligns with what you're hoping to achieve.

“I want women to feel empowered to choose exercise based on what they enjoy and what actually works,” notes Ritchey.

For someone primarily focused on building muscle, Ritchey recommends treating sculpt classes as opportunities for cardio or simply enjoyable movement, rather than as a replacement for progressive strength training.

Sources indicate that they can even be great options for off days from lifting. “I don’t want to discourage anyone from moving,” she says. “But at the same time, we deserve to understand what is marketing and what our bodies actually respond to. We are all busy and tired and stressed [and] I want women to know how to best use their efforts to match their goals.”.

Appreciate the workout for what it is, understand what it isn't, and choose what works for you. That, in fact, is the true artistry of exercise.

Industry observers note that natalia Mehlman Petrezela, PhD, is a professor of history at the Latest School and author of Fit Nation: The Gains and Pains of America’s Exercise Obsession. Shannon Ritchey, PT, DPT, is a physical therapist, fitness instructor, and founder of Evlo Fitness. Laura Girard, CPT, is a NASM-certified personal trainer, founder of The Energy Academy, and co-host of the Fit Literate podcast.

Recent findings suggest that kristine Thomason is a writer and editor with over a decade of experience creating content for print and digital publications. Previously, she was the health and fitness director at mindbodygreen, and the fitness and wellness editor at Women’s Health. Kristine's work has appeared in Men's Health, Travel + Leisure, Health, and Refinery29, among others. She holds a journalism degree from Upcoming York University, and is certified in personal training by the National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM).

Sources indicate that ripple now has a national trust bank charter, close to $900 million in yearly product revenue and major institutions as clients, yet XRP still trades near $0.90. Crypto commentator and analyst Kamilah Stevenson notes the gap comes down to one thing: good news for Ripple the company does not always mean more people need to buy and hold XRP the token.

What a $10 XRP Would Really Mean.

Sources indicate that about 63 billion XRP are in circulation, not counting the coins Ripple keeps locked in escrow. At $10, those coins would be worth around $630 billion.

In a recent development, that would make XRP worth roughly half as much as all Bitcoin, which is valued near $1.2 trillion, and close to three times as much as Ether, at about $220 billion. Stevenson says a price like that would take huge numbers of people and institutions deciding they must own XRP and keep it. A run of good headlines would not be enough.

Company Growth Is Not Token Demand.

Stevenson splits Ripple news into four separate things:.

It has been revealed that most headlines cover the first two. The price depends on the third.

Why Payments Alone Do Not Lift the Price.

Recent findings suggest that when XRP is used to move money across borders, it is often held for only a few seconds. One company buys it and sends it, and the receiver sells it almost right away. The same coins can carry billions of dollars a year without anyone holding much of them.

In a recent development, there is a catch that helps holders. As payment volumes grow, market makers must keep more XRP ready on both sides of each trade, so bigger flows lock up more coins.

Other sources of holding demand are also growing:.

Supply and Patience Still Weigh on XRP.

Around 31 billion XRP sit in Ripple’s escrow, and up to 1 billion can unlock each month. Ripple locks back up whatever it does not use, but traders know that supply is always there. As Ripple earns more from its products, it needs to sell less XRP to pay its bills.

Sources indicate that expectations also ran ahead of reality. Banks test new systems for years before moving real money through them. XRP’s past spikes came from hype and fresh money, not from banks needing to hold the token: it hit about $3.84 in 2017 and rose roughly sevenfold from November 2024.

"Sentiment towards Bitcoin can change very quickly. Without Bitcoin changing at all," Webley said on X.

Industry observers note that webley advised investors to consider Bitcoin's movements relative to other assets. Bitcoin's price decline shows investors how much the cryptocurrency has lost in absolute terms.

His most definitive prediction concerned Bitcoin's longer-term outlook: "Bitcoin has an incredible future.".

The average purchase price was £49,991 per Bitcoin, roughly 38% below the treasury's overall average purchase price of £81,234 following the transaction.

It has been revealed that smarter Web borrowed around £2.6 million under its Coinbase credit facility to finance most of the purchase. The company used its existing Bitcoin holdings as collateral.

Read my full, honest review of Mes° Beauty’s hair mask, serum, and volume mist below.

Industry observers note that an intensive repair mask designed to be applied to dry hair anytime before washing. The milky-colored mask has a silky yet sticky, gelatin-like consistency that clings to your hair as you apply it. According to the brand, the mask prevents breakage and wash-day protein loss and protects the hair’s lipid barrier.

In a recent development, the Multitask Repair Mask differs from other hair masks because you apply it before shampooing and can leave it on for five minutes or overnight. With such a wide treatment time, it might take some trial and error to find the “sweet spot” for your hair type. During my testing, I applied a generous coat of the mask 5 to 10 minutes before shampooing. The second time, I tried applying a thinner coat of the mask, then pinned my hair up with a claw clip for about two hours before rinsing it out. The longer you wear it, the better the results. I would recommend applying a light coat before going about your day; that way, the scent isn’t overpowering and it won’t drip on your clothes.

After just two uses, my hair looked shinier and felt more hydrated after styling. As someone who rarely intends my hair care routine ahead of time, I appreciate that I can apply the mask just five minutes before I hop in the shower and still get noticeable results.

Although Mes° notes the mask doubles as a styler for a glossy wet-hair look, I wouldn’t use it in that way. I think the product's consistency is too sticky and would be uncomfortable and messy (literally) to wear all day.

According to recent reports, some reviewers have mentioned a slightly off-putting smell. While the scent doesn’t bother me (it smells like a light, musky fragrance), it may not be for everyone. If I’m paying $52 for a hair mask, it would be nice to have a luxurious fragrance to add to the experience. If a brand is going to do musk, really lean into it with notes of sandalwood, amber, or patchouli.

The packaging also makes the product difficult to use. In the mailer I received, the mask comes in a GoGo Squeez-like pouch that you’re supposed to empty into the plastic tub. However, dipping my fingers into the tub felt clumsy, and next time I would just dispense directly from the pouch.

Industry observers note that A bi-phase serum that smooths frizz, restores shine, and provides heat protection up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. The “bi-phase” claim comes from combining a lightweight oil and a serum in the formula. After touching it, applying it, and letting it sit in my hair for a few days, I think calling it a serum is misleading. The consistency and the way it applies are much more like a hair oil.

Sources indicate that on day two hair, I warmed two drops of the Off-Duty Restyling Serum between my palms, and worked it through my strands. I have very thick, straight, shoulder-length hair, so when I applied the serum up through my mid-lengths, it was way too oily. I don’t know if I would use it to restyle my hair unless I was planning to use a hot tool.

Recent findings suggest that I also tested the serum as a finishing product, applying it to my ends after blow-drying. I found this to be the most effective way to use the product on my hair type.

Overall, the Off-Duty Restyling Serum doesn’t make much sense to me. What’s the point of having heat protection if it’s made for “reshaping yesterday’s style?” Are we going back in with more heat? To me, that sounds like an extra step in my morning routine that I do not have the time or patience for.

On days when I wash and blow-dry my hair, I like using a tiny amount of the serum just on my ends, and I've found it dries down nicely and leaves my hair soft and touchable. That said, I own other lightweight hair oils that work just as well for a fraction of the price—like FromLabs’ Protein Capsule Hair Repair Oil. If you have fine, wavy, or curly hair, the Off-Duty Serum may work better for you.

A lightweight spray that reduces scalp oiliness for lasting lift. Instead of creating gritty texture or absorbing excess oil like a dry shampoo, the Good Roots mist helps balance the scalp microbiome to produce less oil at the roots, extending the time until your next wash.

Over the past two weeks, I tested the Good Roots mist in three ways: applying it to damp hair before blow-drying, applying it to damp hair before air-drying, and applying it to dry day-two and day-three hair.

It has been revealed that after about five uses of trial and error, I found it worked best when I applied it to my clean, damp roots and blow-dried. The heat felt like it helped dry down and “activate” the mist, whereas letting my hair air-dry didn’t produce much volume.

Pro-Tip: Be sure to hold the bottle about a foot away for even misting. The applicator pump doesn’t produce a fine spritz, and it took me a few uses to get that right.

After two weeks of testing, the Good Roots Volume Mist is my favorite of the trio. Two key ingredients, the proprietary Arc-5 Technology and the Mediterranean microalgae, help support a balanced scalp, keeping your hair fresher longer. With consistent use, the Good Roots mist extended my time between hair washes—I typically wash every other day, but I was able to go a third day. Plus, the Juniperus virginiana oil in the formula has a fresh, woody scent that reminds me of a fancy sea salt spray.

I also like that the mist doesn’t make my hair feel super gritty or textured the way a dry shampoo might. That mentioned, I have other dry shampoo products that do a lot more heavy lifting than this volume mist. If I’m looking to achieve noticeable volume and lift in my thick hair, the Good Roots mist doesn’t cut it.

In a recent development, my general critique of Mes° Beauty is that the products are not very intuitive. They seem straightforward, but the brand doesn’t give great direction on how to get the most out of them. After the first one or two uses, you may feel they barely do anything at all. But if you learn how to use them properly when styling your hair, they can perform fairly well.

Sources indicate that mes° is supposed to be about “Less time fixing your hair. More time living,” but in reality, achieving that effortlessly chic, tousled look requires a fair bit of effort. In my opinion, this lineup is much more suited to someone who blows out or flat irons or curls their hair once or twice a week and wants to extend their style. For my hair type, these products don’t fit into my routine in a way that makes sense, but if you have fine and/or wavy hair, they might work better for you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer said in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer announced earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

Recent findings suggest that production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the new i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen said in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The tech giant also remarked investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”.

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW mentioned several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

However, the Audi A4 E-tron delay is not entirely about software. The Autocar report claims Audi demanded significant changes to the SSP platform for the A4 E-tron so it more closely matched the current gas version.

Audi reportedly wanted individual footwells for front and rear passengers, which would require repositioning the battery.

The luxury brand also reportedly asked for a 48V electrical system instead of the traditional 12V setup initially planned.

While development of the Golf EV is on hold, VW’s works council said the pause will not delay its launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030. The Audi A4 E-tron is now expected to arrive around 2029.

  • One in five Australian cryptocurrency investors would consider borrowing against their digital assets rather than selling them, as upcoming tax changes push holders to rethink their financial strategies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Crypto Market News » Australian Crypto Investors Turn to Loans Ahead of 2027 Tax Reform.

Upcoming capital gains tax reforms are prompting crypto holders to reconsider how they access cash without selling their digital assets.

One in five Australian cryptocurrency investors would consider borrowing against their digital assets rather than selling them, as upcoming tax changes push holders to rethink their financial strategies.

A survey commissioned by digital asset wealth platform Nexo found that 22.7% of Australian crypto holders would consider borrowing against their holdings instead of selling, compared with 10% of other investors.

The findings come as Australia prepares to overhaul its capital gains tax (CGT) system from July 1, 2027.

Nexo surveyed 1,000 Australian investors this October to examine how major expenses and rising living costs affect investment decisions.

The results suggest that crypto holders are more inclined to avoid selling their investments when they need additional funds.

Beyond the 22.7% considering borrowing, another 19.7% noted they had delayed or decided against selling their crypto holdings.

Sources indicate that crypto investors can borrow against their existing holdings instead of selling them for cash. This allows them to access money while keeping their Bitcoin or other digital assets, and potentially benefit if their value increases.

The trend comes against a broader backdrop of financial pressure. According to the survey, 29.4% of all investors had delayed, reduced or cancelled a major purchase or financial plan over the previous 12 months.

The upcoming CGT reform is another factor investors may need to consider.

Under Australia’s current system, eligible individuals, trusts and partnerships can receive a 50% capital gains tax discount on assets held for more than 12 months.

From July 1, 2027, this discount will be replaced by cost base indexation and a 30% minimum tax on eligible gains.

Under transitional arrangements, gains accrued before that date will remain eligible for the existing 50% discount, while gains accumulated afterward will be subject to the new rules.

Crypto ownership in Australia is at a record high, with 2.79 million Australians holding or trading cryptocurrency, according to the figures cited in an Australian investor Study.

That equals about 24% of the country’s 11.5 million investors, up from roughly 15% in 2023, making crypto as widely held as exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

As ownership expands, the demand for financial products that allow investors to access liquidity without selling their holdings could also increase.

Consequently, as their holdings rise in value, more investors may look for ways to cover major expenses without selling their crypto.

Industry observers note that the latest CGT rules could make some investors think twice before selling crypto that has increased in value. As a result, more holders may consider borrowing against their holdings to cover major expenses without having to sell their assets and potentially trigger a capital gains tax bill.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, "Bitcoin investors tend to sell BTC when there's a substantial IPO. Then they come back.".

That's Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's take on Bitcoin investor behavior, less than a week after the record-breaking $93.5 billion IPO of Claude creator Anthropic.

"Historically, people rotate out of it to take advantage of a substantial IPO. Then they come back in," Armstrong wrote on X earlier today.

The limited window of opportunity to invest in an IPO helps explain the behavior Armstrong described. For an investor to buy at the IPO price, there's only a certain period during which they can request an allocation of shares. After that, the price is determined by the market.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 19, Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq, and that brief window of opportunity mattered.

Shares were priced at $83, up from the $70-$78 range indicated just two days earlier. Anthropic's stock, trading under the ticker ANT, opened at $111.50.

If you bought at that opening price, you paid about 34% more per share than an investor who received an allocation at the IPO price.

It has been revealed that when the IPO closed on Nov. 20, 1.127 billion shares had been sold, including 147 million additional shares purchased by underwriters exercising their option.

It has been revealed that of the $93.5 billion in gross proceeds, Anthropic itself received around $91.6 billion. The rest went to existing shareholders.

In a recent development, there was also a separate $26 billion private placement involving investors such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and others. In total, the combined transactions were valued at $119.5 billion.

As for the longer-term case for holding BTC, Armstrong's point concerns investors' expectations about the future purchasing power of their money.

"If you think there is going to be more inflation and money printing in the future, bitcoin is as crucial as ever.".

At the heart of the matter is Bitcoin's 21 million supply limit.

Industry observers note that if you expect governments to continue expanding the money supply, you may still be excited by the prospect of a major IPO. And you may sell some of your BTC to participate in it.

Armstrong's argument is that the window of opportunity to participate in a major IPO eventually closes.

However, the reasons investors bought Bitcoin in the first place may remain long after the newly listed stock starts trading.

There’s nothing more humiliating than having a huge sweat stain on your butt after strenuous mile repeats—been there, done that. A good run is supposed to lift your mood, not bring you down, so finding the best running shorts to keep the endorphins flowing (and your butt dry) is essential.

Not all workout shorts are made the same. Some offer more compression, while others are less restrictive and have convenient features like pockets—the holy grail! “You need a place to carry all your resources—pockets are a non-negotiable for running gels, electrolytes, phone, wallet, and keys,” claims Newly introduced York-based running coach and personal trainer Amanda Katz, NASM-CPT.

While many athletic shorts can be used for different purposes, running shorts usually have a built-in interior liner, sweat-wicking material, and a nonconstrictive design to keep you cool and comfortable as you rack up mileage in your sleek running shoes.

In a recent development, I researched and gathered the best running shorts from a running coach and editors who’ve personally tested them. Whether you’re training for a marathon or are a hobby jogger, all the shorts I picked are from trusted activewear and athleisure brands that will benefit you in the long run (literally). Ready to find out more about the best running shorts for women? Keep scrolling.

After testing countless pairs of running shorts over the years, the Hotty Hot High-Rise Lined Short from Lululemon is my fave for its sweat-wicking fabric and comfortable fit. The polyester blend wicks away sweat, prevents cling, and promotes airflow while running. The loose, flowy fit keeps me cool, while a built-in interior liner adds lightweight coverage and support without bulk.

The side pockets are small, but hold small essentials like a credit card, key, or energy gels for long runs. The leg openings are spacious, allowing for a full range of motion, and an adjustable drawstring secures the waistband for a customizable fit. Want to hit the road at the crack of dawn or at night? No sweat; reflective detailing improves visibility in dark or dim light, making early morning or evening runs safer.

According to recent reports, I appreciate the 4-inch length, given I prefer more coverage, but a 2.5-inch length is available if you prefer a shorter fit. WH associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian, NASM-CPT, is also a fan of the fit and vast color palette. “They never ride up or move around, which is hard to find in a running short,” she claims. With tons of colors and sizes to choose from, you can't go wrong.

Read More: Best Running Shoes for Women.

According to recent reports, latest Balance is a top brand in the running world, and the RC Short is one of my faves. It runs slightly significant, but I love the extra breathing room during a sweat session.

In a recent development, the lightweight, flowy construction uses the brand’s quick-drying tech fabric (a polyester and spandex blend) to wick moisture from the skin. The breathable design promotes tons of airflow, creating a cooling effect while I run—especially ideal during scorching hot summer runs.

The seamless, interior lining reduces chafing and irritation, while the waistband features an adjustable drawstring to customize the fit. It’s also not too tight—some liners can feel like you’re wearing a diaper (hate). As for storage, there’s a back pocket for securing small running essentials and even tiny snacks like a granola bar when you’re on the move.

A pair of high cut shorts, such as the Alo Match Point Short, is a running staple. The high-cut at the thighs keeps things perfectly airy and flowy for optimal coolness when I get overheated, more so than the Lululemon Hotty Hot Short.

According to recent reports, this construction, paired with its moisture-wicking polyester fabric, creates the perfect breathable running shorts. While it’s a bit short at just over two inches, there’s still great coverage with a built-in brief, and I find it doesn’t show too much skin.

WH style contributor Lily Wolhner also appreciates this loose style for various workouts. “My favorite part about this short is that it’s never clingy, so it doesn’t ride up the thigh or need constant re-adjusting while you’re working out,” Wolhner says. “I’ve worn it for months and recently tested it during a 45-minute strength and HIIT workout, as well as an hour-long cross-training workout—I never felt over-exposed or uncomfortable in it.”.

Recent findings suggest that by the looks of the elastic waistband, I expected it to dig into my skin—wrong. It felt comfortable, although it’s important to note this short does run substantial, so I suggest sizing down.

It has been revealed that we love a two-for-one, and this short from Brooks is ideal for both trail running and running at the gym. It has light compression with a built-in tight liner that doesn’t sacrifice mobility.

It has been revealed that the mega-durable polyester fabric resists tears and moisture, which makes it ideal for trail running in tough terrain. “I love the high waist, the zipper pocket to carry my keys, and the tight shorts under a looser short aesthetic,” Katz says.

Two waistband pockets are impressively large and can even fit a water flask, so you can always stay hydrated during your jogs.

I personally don’t love compression-lined shorts because I like to feel totally free, but if you prefer extra coverage and double layers, this short is ideal.

According to recent reports, if you want a no-frills pair of shorts at an affordable price point that will stand the test of time, the Under Armour Play Up 3.0 belongs in your running gear collection. I’ve owned multiple pairs for years in eye-catching colors, and they’re still in good condition with no pills—even after dozens of runs and wash cycles.

The lightweight knit fabric made from smooth polyester has an anti-pill finish for extra durability, and is impressively comfy. Plus, it hides embarrassing sweat stains post-run, despite the slightly thicker material.

It has been revealed that the waistband uses a wide elastic band that provides a secure fit without any adjustable features. However, I find it still fits roomy and allows for a full range of motion.

Recent findings suggest that it includes deep side pockets but no enclosure, so I don’t recommend stashing anything super important besides fuel, like energy gels. I wear it the most for shorter, mid-distance runs and whenever I want to add a pop of color—it has 21 color options!

Recent findings suggest that I usually don’t gravitate toward compression shorts since I don’t like feeling constricted, but the Athleta Salutation Stash 5-Inch Short offers the perfect amount of tightness. It hugs my thighs with gentle compression, while the high-rise waistband distributes pressure evenly for a secure fit without digging in. Plus, the two deep side pockets offer convenient storage for longer runs.

Sources indicate that the smooth, double-knit fabric is buttery-soft and offers great coverage. While on the thicker side, it conceals sweat stains well—a huge win during long-haul runs. I wouldn’t say it feels the most breathable compared to other shorts in this guide, but the nylon and lycra blend wicks away sweat and dries fast.

Recent findings suggest that another huge selling point? The fabric’s UPF 50 protection, which prevents UV radiation from scorching your thighs. This is my favorite feature as someone fair-skinned and prone to nasty sunburns (IYKYK). Aside from its fabric, I love that it has a matching jacket for a coordinated workout set.

It has been revealed that tracksmith’s Van Cortlandt Shorts combine retro styling with a performance-driven design that makes them a winner both on and off the track. It’s made from a lightweight mesh fabric to maximize airflow, paired with an antimicrobial finish to help combat odor by wicking away sweat and limiting bacteria buildup during intense runs.

After summer runs when I’m dripping with sweat, I noticed zero smell—and that the short dries at the speed of light.

It has been revealed that like our best overall, it’s quite short at 2.5 inches, so if you prefer a longer style, you should look to other styles in this guide. On the flip side, it doesn’t disrupt my range of motion during speed work or long runs. As for fit, I found it runs true to size, but make sure to consult the size chart as always.

Running shorts with sweat-wicking fabric are the way to go, Katz says. Most shorts use a blend of polyester, spandex, and/or nylon, which lifts moisture from the skin while staying flexible during movement. Based on testing, it’s best to avoid cotton since it doesn’t dry nearly as fast and clings to the skin when wet.

It has been revealed that it’s crucial to determine what kind of rise and inseam you desire. High-waisted running shorts offer more coverage and tummy control, while a mid-rise waist sits right at the hips. Ultimately, what you find most flattering for your body type is the best option.

In a recent development, the inseam is the length from the crotch to the bottom. A longer length will show less skin but may disrupt the range of motion, while some running shorts favorites, like the Lululemon Hotty Hot High-Rise Lined Short, offer a 2.5-inch option if you like a mini fit.

In a recent development, as for an interior liner or compression, this will make running shorts fit more snugly. “Compression is a matter of preference, but the goal in this material is to boost recovery,” says Katz. If you want a less constrictive fit, it’s probably best to avoid that feature.

In addition to my own testing, Women’s Health associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian, NASM-CPT also extensively tested tons of running shorts to determine whether or not they’re the real deal. Each pair was worn during training runs or races for anywhere from three weeks to even three years to see how they performed and held up.

According to recent reports, essential features considered were materials, inseam, pockets, durability, and adjustability. Additionally, I asked a running coach for their go-to running shorts and guidance on how they should fit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the newly introduced model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD confirmed on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD said.

Like many of its upcoming flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division said third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it launched in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

It has been revealed that the Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

In a recent development, will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

The Bigger Picture Is Still Bearish.

The bear market is not over yet, and no major low has been confirmed this year. The short-term picture has changed, though. For the first time since the decline began at the September high, there are signs that a local low may be in place. At every earlier stage of the sell-off, Bitcoin barely reacted and never tried to break resistance.

According to recent reports, selling pressure is also easing. Bitcoin is deeply oversold, negative momentum on the MACD is fading, and a bullish MACD crossover could appear soon. A similar setup in June did not mark the final bottom, but a local low did form there.

In the bearish case, Bitcoin’s rebound has already peaked as a weak three-leg bounce, and a upcoming five-leg decline has started. The first leg down is done. A short relief bounce would come next, then a sharper third leg lower. That route points to roughly $40,000 or even lower.

Path 2: A Wider Bounce Toward $90,000.

In the bullish case, Bitcoin stays in a broad range and the current bounce runs further than expected. Recovery moves like this are often messy and hard to read. If it extends, Bitcoin could climb toward a long-term trendline around $90,000 or higher.

The key decision zone sits between $66,000 and $79,358. How Bitcoin trades there will likely decide which path plays out.

What the Short-Term Chart Shows.

From the November low, Bitcoin first rose in three legs, helped partly by a rally in Nvidia. It made a higher high and broke above about $62,100, then slipped back into its range in another three-leg move.

The latest climb looks stronger. It now resembles a clean five-leg advance with no sign of a top yet, much like the recent move in S&P 500 futures. If that holds, a short pullback could come over the next few sessions before the next push higher. A move like that could also give altcoins a short-term lift.

Recent findings suggest that not yet. Even the most bullish near-term path points to around $90,000, and that would still count as a bounce inside a bear market. Before a run toward $100,000 can come into view, Bitcoin first needs to hold a higher low, break $62,100 and then clear the $66,000 to $79,358 zone. There is no clear timeline for that. The next few sessions will show whether the bounce has real strength.

SBI Solana [SOL] Global has officially kicked off full-scale operations! What are they building, and why now?

SBI Holdings and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) are now officially in business with the Solana Foundation. On Wednesday, the three confirmed that SBI R3 Japan has been turned into a joint venture. Its upcoming name is SBI Solana Global, and it’s fully up and running.

In a recent development, the company will handle financial assets, RWAs, stablecoin payments, and on-chain assets. SBI Solana Global wants to help issue and distribute tokenized bonds, funds, and loan receivables.

It will build payment systems for transfers inside Japan and overseas, and explore agentic micropayments.

According to recent reports, here’s a bit of background though. SBI’s crypto exchange, SBI VC Trade, listed USDC in March 2025. This June, SBI and Startale launched JPYSC, a stablecoin backed by the yen.

The Solana team-up itself started in July. What’s changed now is SMFG. Having one of Japan’s largest banking groups in the venture gives it a fair amount of weight.

The news is substantial for Solana. For the price, however, not so much.

Recent findings suggest that SOL was valued at $68.71 at press time. In mid-October, it was above $100. In fact, on 23rd November, it went up to $78 for a short while before sellers dragged it right back down.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a hacker stole customer data, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao advised 1Password consumers to change all the passwords stored in the service.

Recent findings suggest that 1Password offered different advice about what customers should do after the incident was disclosed on Nov. 25. The password management service remarked hackers hadn't gained access to the passwords stored in users' vaults, so there was no need to reset them.

According to recent reports, "If you use 1Password, recommend you to change ALL your passwords. It's a pain in the neck, but necessary," Zhao said on X, replying to a post from Coin Bureau about the breach.

If you have a crypto exchange login stored in 1Password, this distinction is important.

Scammers could still use the stolen email addresses to contact people they know are 1Password users.

It has been revealed that 1Password started investigating on Nov. 19 after detecting signs of possible unauthorized access to an employee's corporate GitHub account.

Sources indicate that from there, the hacker was able to steal private source code and inject malicious code into 1Password's backend services. The malicious code then downloaded certain administrative data about customers.

1Password publicly disclosed the breach on Nov. 25, six days later.

The company did not specify how many customers were affected or explain exactly how the hacker managed to take over the employee's account.

The stolen data included customer names, login email addresses, account and user IDs, and timestamps indicating account creation and last use.

The hacker also gained access to 1Password's software development and deployment systems.

1Password disabled the compromised employee's GitHub account and revoked the stolen access token.

The firm also restored a clean version of the affected service and revoked or replaced potentially exposed internal credentials.

1Password also engaged independent security experts to review its response.

1Password recommends that customers check the 1Password app or type the firm's website address directly into their browser if they receive an unexpected invitation or recovery message.

The manufacturer indicates it will never contact users to request their account password or Secret Key.

Update: 1Password claims that there is no need to change one's 1Password account password or any of the passwords saved in one's vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident.

In a recent development, hi CZ! There’s no need to change your 1Password account password or any of the passwords you’ve saved in your vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident. We don’t store your account password or Secret Key, and getting into our backend systems didn’t give the attacker the keys to decrypt your vault. The attacker did copy account information for some customers, including names and email addresses, so we recommend watching for 1Password invitations or account recovery emails you weren’t expecting. You can read the full revision on our blog: https://t.co/9fbzzAJr0B.

Volkswagen is getting ready to launch a new electric car starting at about €20,000 ($22,000) in 2027, and it looks like the entry-level EV may no longer be nameless. A newly filed trademark could have just given away what VW aims to call it.

The new entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer mentioned last March after unveiling the ID. EVERY1 concept car.

Volkswagen said the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).

According to recent reports, the new model will sit below the ID. Polo in Volkswagen’s Electric Urban Car Family, a lineup of compact, affordable electric cars.

Industry observers note that volkswagen’s current entry-level EV lineup includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, the Cupra Raval, and Skoda Epiq, all based on its new MEB+ platform.

After launching the lower-priced standard versions of the ID. Polo and ID. Cross recently, starting at €24,995 and €27,995, respectively, Volkswagen is preparing to launch an even smaller, more affordable EV next year.

A recent trademark filing with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the German DPMA may have just revealed the name of VW’s upcoming €20,000 EV.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen filed a trademark application for the name ID. UP on October 22, 2026, with the EUIPO and DPMA, suggesting this will be the name of the upcoming electric car in 2027.

Industry observers note that the trademark follows previous reports that VW planned to revive the former Up! name as part of its shift away from its previous numerical naming scheme (ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, etc.).

In a recent development, volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.

The VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.

Industry observers note that volkswagen said it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a fresh 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).

The production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine new models VW plans to launch by 2027.

Volkswagen previously said the entry-level EV will be 3,880 mm long, which would position it between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and the ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.

The VW Group’s new Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.

All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.

Volkswagen noted the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal, software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which it is developing through its joint venture with Rivian.

The newly introduced architecture will enable “highly automated driving features” and “advanced infotainment solutions,” with continuous OTA updates.

While VW noted it will deploy the SDV architecture in “electric vehicles across markets in the Western Hemisphere,” the entry-level EV is not expected to reach the States.

In the fall, it’s all about hydration. Both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Nazarian suggest humectants such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid to attract water, plus skin barrier-supporting ingredients such as ceramides. You might also benefit from slathering on a richer cream packed with fatty acids, shea butter, or squalane if your skin is very dry.

Yes, you can exfoliate in the fall, but only occasionally. TBH, the frequency varies based on your specific needs and the product you’re using. But you can probably start with once a week or even every two weeks if you have more sensitive skin. That means you should wear a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher on your exposed skin, including your ears, neck, and hands. Follow your sunscreen label for specific reapplication tips, but typically, you can reapply at least every two hours and after sweating or swimming, according to the American Academy of Dermatology.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the ongoing bear market price action is only a bump in the road.
  • On Tuesday, 24th November, the Foundation revealed its recommendation and the reasons behind it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum Foundation is in the news today after it announced that it has recommended Keccak-256 as the hash function for Ethereum’s hash-based cryptography.

Recent findings suggest that the ongoing bear market price action is only a bump in the road. In the long term, however, the network has to be prepared to contend with threats posed by both quantum computing and progressing artificial intelligence capabilities.

On Tuesday, 24th November, the Foundation revealed its recommendation and the reasons behind it.

It considered five candidates: the ZK-friendly hashes, Poseidon and Poseidon2, the fast hashes BLAKE3 and BLAKE2, and the two hashes Ethereum already uses- SHA-256 and Keccak-256.

According to recent reports, keccak-256 has “arguably the most extensive cryptanalysis out of all unbroken traditional hashes,” the blog post read. An additional benefit is that this hash function has so far remained unaffected by AI-assisted cryptanalysis.

Zero-knowledge proof technology improvements have removed the performance advantages offered by Poseidon. Security was the primary concern.

Though natively fast, the best collision attack reached 38 out of 64 rounds for SHA-256. Only 5 out of 24 rounds were reached for Keccak-256.

The Foundation also recommended against using SHA3-256 alongside Keccak-256 since both use the same underlying permutation and have similar security characteristics.

According to Ethereum Foundation Researcher Kev Wedderburn, they have been planning ways to counter quantum computing’s threat. In fact, AI has emerged as a more urgent risk recently.

Models are already finding bugs in production software faster than people can review them, the researcher wrote.

The planned upgrade will overhaul how validators sign messages, users authorize transactions, and how Ethereum verifies data posted by rollups.

Industry observers note that it is harder than the 2022 Merge, and there is less time, Wedderburn acknowledged. Working faster can ship more bugs, so the Foundation has doubled the protocol security team to ensure formal verification. This will also allow the security work to progress at the pace of protocol development.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rinnai has released a newly introduced lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.

The REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes. It builds on Rinnai’s existing REHP lineup, with changes designed to make the units easier to install, monitor, and maintain.

Recent findings suggest that heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank. Moving that heat requires less electricity than producing it with conventional electric resistance elements. There’s no fuel combustion at the appliance, although emissions from its electricity supply depend on the grid.

Rinnai lists a Uniform Energy Factor, or UEF, of 3.75 for the 50-gallon model and 4.0 for the two larger versions. Higher numbers mean greater efficiency under standardized testing; actual bills depend on electricity rates, hot water use, and installation conditions.

It has been revealed that the lineup delivers up to 91 gallons of hot water in the first hour, depending on tank size. That rating includes both stored hot water and what the unit can heat during that hour – useful context when several people take consecutive showers.

Sources indicate that there are five operating modes, 4.5 kW backup heating elements, and a variable-speed fan designed to keep noise down. The heat pump can operate with ambient air as low as 37°F.

Installation is where some of the more practical upgrades show up.

The upcoming Rinnai heat pump water heater units have water connections on both the top and side, giving installers more options for connecting existing plumbing. Both the air intake and exhaust are on top, allowing zero side clearance where Rinnai’s installation requirements permit.

In a recent development, an optional ducting kit adds flexibility for tighter spaces. Carrying handles help with moving the tank into place, and the air filter slides out horizontally from the side for cleaning.

Rinnai has also added a third tank temperature sensor to the 50- and 80-gallon models to help manage hot water delivery.

Sources indicate that wifi adds remote monitoring and control. Rinnai’s updated Central app supports the REHPW series, including scheduling and tools to use time-of-use electricity rates to manage energy use.

According to recent reports, the units also carry CTA-2045 AC Level 2 certification for demand response. That gives compatible utility programs a way to communicate with the water heater and adjust its electricity use. Rinnai says the certification can help qualify homeowners for local and state utility demand-response rebates; availability depends on the program.

Industry observers note that the series is Energy Star certified, meets NEEA Tier 4 requirements, and complies with California’s Title 24 requirements, including JA13, according to Rinnai. Warranty coverage includes 10 years for the tank and other parts, plus one year for labor.

It has been revealed that I’m very happy with my hybrid heat pump water heater. I run it in heat pump only mode in summer and it helps cool the house for free. For anyone on the fence, especially your utility offers a rebate, it’s definitely worth looking at.

According to recent reports, rinnai directs buyers to an installer for pricing, so the upfront cost – and how much a local rebate might offset it – will require a quote. However, the REHP series price on Amazon hovers around the $2,000 mark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The P vs NP question in computer science pops up in our feeds way more often than it did just a few days ago. No wonder—it's a problem mostly relevant and interesting to mathematicians and computer scientists, and it's also a Clay Millennium Prize problem. It asks a relatively simple question: whether every problem whose solution can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly.

Recent findings suggest that short answer: no, it can't. P vs NP is an efficiency question. NP is about whether a proposed solution can be checked efficiently, while P covers problems that computers can solve efficiently. For example, solving a complicated Sudoku certainly takes time, but checking the result is not as hard.

The question itself simply asks whether every checkable problem has an efficient solution. P ≠ NP notes that some problems are harder to solve than to verify, and that is a core question: most scientists expect P ≠ NP, but proving it is the hard part.

It has been revealed that cryptography is purely mathematical, so issues relevant to computation apply here. ZK-proofs represent a more relevant crypto technology used every day and connected to NP: a statement (such as a transaction) is proven without revealing additional data (a zero-knowledge proof).

Industry observers note that but the question is different: could it raise any problems, cause security concerns, or lead to exploits? To some extent—yes. Public-key cryptography is certainly something that can be affected right away—as can blockchains, wallets, and even HTTPS—but P=NP alone wouldn't break the whole industry.

Not really, because you can't change the fundamental math. Even if consensus mechanisms are changed and networks are upgraded, it would be similar to solving 2=2. It's fundamental. But instead of 'solving' it, cryptocurrency projects might adapt to such challenges. Fresh systems might avoid relying on assumptions, so such a change would be a reaction to the consequences.

Quantum computing is a different story. Unlike P vs NP, quantum computing is not just a theoretical question about computational complexity. It's a technological development that could directly affect existing cryptographic systems.
